title: Complexes with cohomology in a single degree
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] fixed setting),
let $T$ be a separated
finite-type $k$-scheme, let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(T,\Lambda)$ and let
$r\in\mathbf Z$.

1. *concentration in one degree.* If the
[def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] cohomology sheaves
$\mathcal H^i(K)$ vanish for every $i\neq r$, then the
truncation triangles induce a canonical isomorphism
$$
K\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;\mathcal H^r(K)[-r].
$$
1. *local constancy detected on an etale cover.* Let
$u:U\to T$ be a surjective
etale morphism and suppose
that $Lu^*K\cong\underline L[-r]$ for a
locally constant
$\Lambda$-sheaf $\underline L$ with finite stalks on $U$.
Then $\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ for every $i\neq r$, and
$\mathcal H^r(K)$ is locally constant with finite stalks on
$T$.

proof.text: Choose a cochain representative of $K$ and apply the following canonical constructions; the functoriality assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle] ensures that their derived maps are the canonical truncation maps. Let $c_r:\tau_{\leq r}K\to K$ be the canonical truncation inclusion and let $j_r:\tau_{\leq r}K\to\mathcal H^r(K)[-r]$ be the map supplied by the truncation triangle. By [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-cohomology], $c_r$ induces isomorphisms on cohomology in degrees $i\leq r$ and $\tau_{\leq r}K$ has zero cohomology for $i>r$. The hypothesis gives $\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ for $i>r$, so $c_r$ induces isomorphisms in every degree. The explicit kernel/image description of $j_r$ in [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle], together with the same truncation calculation, shows that $\mathcal H^i(j_r)$ is an isomorphism in every degree: at $i=r$ it is the cycles-to-cohomology quotient, and for $i\ne r$ both source and target vanish. The cohomology-sheaf interpretation is [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves].

By [lem-weil-pbc-unbounded-derived-iso-cohomology], a morphism in the derived category is an isomorphism when it induces isomorphisms on all cohomology sheaves. Hence both $c_r$ and $j_r$ are isomorphisms, and their composite $j_r\circ c_r^{-1}:K\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathcal H^r(K)[-r]$ is canonical and functorial in $K$.

Work with $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$, the finite-torsion setting stipulated by [def-pur-conventions]; the other coefficient versions are the separate transports specified there. Clause (4) of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] states explicitly that $A_{E,n}$ is a finite local ring, so the finite discrete coefficient hypotheses below hold. Since $u:U\to T$ is etale and surjective, the singleton family $\{u\}$ is a pro-etale covering by [lem-pur-etale-proetale-cover]. By [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact], inverse image on these constant-coefficient module sheaves is exact. On a cochain representative it preserves kernels, images, and their quotient, hence sends $\Ker d^i/\Im d^{i-1}$ to $\Ker(u^*d^i)/\Im(u^*d^{i-1})$ and sends quasi-isomorphisms to quasi-isomorphisms. Thus termwise $u^*$ computes $Lu^*$ and gives $u^*\mathcal H^i(K)\cong\mathcal H^i(Lu^*K)$. The assumed isomorphism with $\underline L[-r]$ makes this zero for $i\ne r$. The covering-family clause of [lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative], applied to $\{u\}$, gives $\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ for $i\ne r$.

Put $G=\mathcal H^r(K)$, so step 3 gives $u^*G\cong\underline L$. We check that this is also the localized restriction $G|_U$, rather than silently identifying the two sites. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], $U_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is $T_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$, with the restricted constant coefficient ring. For an object $V\to U$, the pairs $(W,\phi:V\to U\times_TW)$ in the inverse-image formula of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] are precisely $T$-maps $V\to W$. Their category has initial object $(V,\mathrm{graph}(V\to U))$, since $V\to T$ is a valid object by the localization lemma. Indeed an arrow from this pair to $(W,\phi)$ must be the $T$-map $V\to W$ obtained by projecting $\phi$, and this map satisfies the required equality by the fibre-product universal property. Its opposite therefore has a terminal object, and the displayed colimit is $G(V)$. These identifications commute with restriction maps. This presheaf is already a sheaf by the site equivalence, so sheafification leaves it unchanged. The coefficient identification is the identity on constant sections, hence respects the transported module actions of [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact]. Thus $u^*G\cong G|_U$ as module sheaves, and $G|_U\cong\underline L$.

Choose a pro-etale covering $\{v_j:V_j\to U\}$ trivializing $\underline L$, as in [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf]. The localization equivalence of [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization] identifies its constant module models and restrictions with those in $T_{\mathrm{proet}}/U$: both are the sheafifications of the same constant presheaves on the identified sites. The composite family $\{u\circ v_j:V_j\to T\}$ is a covering by the composition axiom in [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], applied to the singleton cover from step 3. On each $V_j$ the restriction of $G$ is the corresponding constant model of $\underline L$, by step 4 and evaluation of iterated restriction at $W\to V_j$. This is exactly local constancy of $G$ on $T$.

Finally let $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to T$ be any geometric point. The singleton etale cover lifts it to $\bar u:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to U$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-cover-geometric-point-lift]. Use the representative-and-refinement description of stalks and the filtered opposite neighbourhood category in [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], forgetting the map to $U$ sends a pointed neighbourhood of $\bar u$ to one of $\bar t$, and defines a map $(G|_U)_{\bar u}\to G_{\bar t}$. It is surjective: a representative $s\in G(W)$ restricts to $W\times_TU$, pointed by $(\bar w,\bar u)$, which is a neighbourhood over $U$ by the localization lemma. It is injective: if representatives on pointed neighbourhoods $V_1,V_2$ over $U$ become equal in $G_{\bar t}$, filteredness gives a pointed common refinement $R\to V_1,V_2$ where the sections agree. The two composites $R\rightrightarrows U$ preserve the chosen point; the equalization condition gives a further pointed refinement $R'\to R$ on which these composites agree. With that common map to $U$, both $R'\to V_i$ are $U$-morphisms, so the representatives already agree in $(G|_U)_{\bar u}$. These sectionwise restriction maps preserve the module operations. Thus $G_{\bar t}\cong(G|_U)_{\bar u}\cong\underline L_{\bar u}$, which is finite by hypothesis. This proves finiteness of every geometric stalk without a uniform bound on their sizes; on the empty scheme the assertion is vacuous.

In the purity conventions of [def-pur-conventions],
let $T$ be a separated
finite-type $k$-scheme, let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(T,\Lambda)$ and let
$r\in\mathbf Z$.

1. *concentration in one degree.* If the
[def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] cohomology sheaves
$\mathcal H^i(K)$ vanish for every $i\neq r$, then the
truncation triangles induce a canonical isomorphism
$$
K\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;\mathcal H^r(K)[-r].
$$
1. *local constancy detected on an etale cover.* Let
$u:U\to T$ be a surjective
etale morphism and suppose
that $Lu^*K\cong\underline L[-r]$ for a
locally constant
$\Lambda$-sheaf $\underline L$ with finite stalks on $U$.
Then $\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ for every $i\neq r$, and
$\mathcal H^r(K)$ is locally constant with finite stalks on
$T$.

proof.text:
Step 1: the truncation triangles. By
[def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves] the sheaves
$\mathcal H^i(K)$ are the cohomology sheaves for the standard
t-structure, and for every $a\in\mathbf Z$ there are exact triangles
$\tau_{\leq a-1}K\to\tau_{\leq a}K\to\mathcal H^a(K)[-a]\to$ and
$\tau_{\leq a}K\to K\to\tau_{\geq a+1}K\to$. A complex all of whose
cohomology sheaves vanish is zero in the derived category of
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], that category being the
localization at the quasi-isomorphisms. If therefore
$\mathcal H^i(K)=0$ for every $i\neq r$, then
$\tau_{\geq r+1}K\simeq0$ and $\tau_{\leq r-1}K\simeq0$, and the two
triangles exhibit $K$ and $\mathcal H^r(K)[-r]$ as models of one
and the same object; this is (1).
Step 2: an etale cover. Pullback of sheaves is exact, so the derived
pullback $Lu^*$ commutes with cohomology sheaves, and etale
morphisms are weakly etale, hence covering families in the sense of
[def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] (an etale morphism is flat with
flat diagonal, which is the description of weakly etale in
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]); the description of etale
morphisms is that of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Since $u$ is a
member of a pro-etale covering family, inverse image along $u$
reflects vanishing of a sheaf, by clause (1) of
[lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative]; as $Lu^*K\cong \underline L[-r]$ has cohomology only in degree $r$, the sheaves
$u^*\mathcal H^i(K)\cong\mathcal H^i(Lu^*K)$ vanish for $i\neq r$,
and therefore so do the sheaves $\mathcal H^i(K)$. For the remaining
degree, $u^*\mathcal H^r(K)\cong\underline L$ is constant along the
covering $u$, so $\mathcal H^r(K)$ is locally constant in the sense
recalled in [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]; the stalks of a
constructible object may be computed at geometric points, by part (3) of
[lem-cbc-proetale-stalk-conservative], and they are the stalks of
$\underline L$ there, hence finite. This is (2).
